transcript:
[doctor] Hi Mr. Li, how are you feeling today?

[patient] Not too well, Doctor. I've been having this severe, sharp pain in my left flank for the past 5 days.

[doctor] I'm sorry to hear that. Can you describe the pain a bit more for me?

[patient] It's really severe and sharp. It’s been so bad that I can’t do my daily activities or go to work.

[doctor] I see. Have you noticed any other symptoms along with the pain?

[patient] Yes, I’ve had some blood in my urine and I’ve been vomiting. I also think I have a slight fever.

[doctor] Okay, that sounds quite uncomfortable. Have you been able to sleep at night?

[patient] No, not really. The pain keeps me up.

[doctor] Hmm, I understand. Have you had any issues with your stomach or digestion?

[patient] Just the vomiting. It happens every now and then.

[doctor] Alright. And how about your urination? Aside from the blood, any other issues?

[patient] Just the sharp pain in my left flank and the blood in my urine.

[doctor] Got it. I also see here in your records that you have a history of gout. Could you tell me more about that?

[patient] Yes, I’ve had gout for a while now. It makes it hard to exercise because of the pain.

[doctor] I see. And what’s your diet like?

[patient] I eat a lot of high-protein and purine-rich foods. I know I shouldn’t, but I really enjoy them.

[doctor] Alright, and how about your lifestyle? Do you smoke or drink?

[patient] Yes, I smoke about a pack a day and have around 6-8 drinks per week. I also enjoy fishing and playing chess.

[doctor] Thank you for sharing that. It’s important for us to get a full picture. Let me check your vitals now.

[patient] Sure.

[doctor] Your blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, heart rate is 85 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and your temperature is 99.2°F.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] I’m also going to do a physical exam. Let’s start with your abdomen. Please let me know if you feel any pain.

[patient] Sure.

[doctor] (palpating) Do you feel any tenderness here in your left flank?

[patient] Yes, it’s quite tender there.

[doctor] Alright. Your genitourinary exam appears normal. We are currently awaiting the results of your CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to determine the size and location of any kidney stones.

[patient] Okay, I hope we get some answers soon.

[doctor] Based on your symptoms and history, it seems like you might have a kidney stone. We’ll confirm once we get the CT results.

[patient] That makes sense. What can we do in the meantime?

[doctor] For now, I’m going to prescribe Allopurinol 100 mg daily for 30 days to help reduce your uric acid levels. 

[patient] Okay, I can do that.

[doctor] It’s also very important that you increase your water intake to 3-4 liters a day.

[patient] That’s a lot of water, but I’ll try.

[doctor] It will help flush out the stone. We’re also referring you to a pain management specialist to help manage your chronic pain.

[patient] That would be great. The pain is really hard to deal with.

[doctor] I understand. We also need to talk about some lifestyle changes. Reducing high-protein and purine-rich foods can help prevent future stones and gout attacks.

[patient] I’ll try my best, Doctor.

[doctor] It’s also crucial to consider quitting smoking and reducing your alcohol consumption.

[patient] I know, I’ve been meaning to cut down.

[doctor] We can provide resources to help you with that. It’s important for your overall health.

[patient] Okay, I’ll give it a try.

[doctor] Excellent. We’ll schedule a follow-up visit in 2 weeks to review your imaging results and see how you’re responding to the treatment.

[patient] Sounds good. Thank you, Doctor.

[doctor] You’re welcome. Do you have any other questions or concerns right now?

[patient] No, I think that covers everything.

[doctor] Great. Take care, Mr. Li, and we’ll see you in 2 weeks.

[patient] Thank you, Doctor.
